items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: it was Jimmy Knepper’s album and Al and Zoot were on it

ctx.x: Yes, and then of course the engineer and the producer can take those ten tracks and they can create a new one. That’s a favorite thing, you know, like take a piece — the first four bars from this one —

Yeah. I hear it on records. This one record I played on it with Gene Roland arrangements, it was Jimmy Knepper’s album and Al and Zoot were on it and Clark Terry, Snooky Young. And swinging. Called “Swinging Friends” was the name of the record. And sometimes — well in particular the last chorus like a totally different tempo because of a splice, you know a bad splice, because of an ensemble problem you know. Maybe it wasn’t clean so they just like spliced in the last chorus in a totally different tempo from…
could tell that he learned the piece from a recording that had a mistake in it. You know. Bad splice.
